quotes.text: So the Lower Spring sent a smaller measure—not nothing, for that would end all possibility, but not the generous gift of before.
"Show me through your return that your actions match your words. Then, perhaps, the true dance can begin again."
Having shown trust and received hollow reciprocity, it could not sustain the cycle alone. With heavy heart, it returned nothing.
The betrayer must prove consistency through many dawns. The betrayed must risk trust again, incrementally.
"You write beautiful myths about reciprocity," the Lower Spring said to the mountain winds.
The mountains learned: someone must be first to thaw.
The Lower Spring, wounded, returned that betrayal with silence, teaching the lesson of consequence.

note: Random forced zeros become Higher Spring betrayal and Lower Spring's silence; smaller-but-not-nothing test, then rebuilt three-for-three rhythm.

quotes.text: When the cycle of reciprocity breaks, when generosity meets with less than was given, the waters stop flowing."
First it sent barely two vessels—testing. The Higher Spring returned abundantly. Then it sent slightly more—still testing.
It kept all nine, returning nothing. "Let the betrayer taste what betrayal feels like," it whispered bitterly.
Neither Spring gave blindly, but both gave fully.
"I betrayed your courage when you gave three vessels, creating nine. I kept nearly all.
My myths spoke of honor while my waters spoke of greed."
